topic: How does gateway separation distance affect spatial correlation and link budget margins in Q/V band feeder links?
consensus_response: Increased gateway separation distance (d km) leads to reduced spatial correlation between gateways, resulting in increased rain attenuation variability on feeder links. This strain on the link budget can be mitigated by using multiple gateways for transmit diversity techniques, but at the cost of increased complexity and potential interference. The physical mechanism of array factor and interference effects due to gateway separation is captured by the spatial correlation coefficient (ρ) formula: ρ = 0.94 exp(−d/30) + 0.06 exp[−(d/500)].
reference_context: The reference context provides factual ground-truth about Q/V band feeder links, including the impact of rain attenuation, lognormal distribution, and spatial correlation coefficient (ρ) on link budget margins.
